prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
## Main Story

AI is moving quickly, but the rules are trying to keep up.

In Europe, legal duties for general-purpose AI models started on 2 August 2025. Other parts of the EU AI Act began enforcement on 2 August 2026. These include rules on prohibited AI practices, some transparency duties, and certain duties for general-purpose models. But the timetable is staged. Not every rule began on the same day.

International action is also growing, but it has a different role. The United Nations created an independent scientific panel with 40 members in August 2025. In a preliminary report released in July 2026, the panel warned that current safeguards cannot keep pace with the growth of AI capabilities. But the panel does not make or enforce international law.

The technology itself is also advancing. In cyber evaluations, one institute found that the best models completed apprentice-level tasks about 50% of the time, compared with just over 10% in early 2024. The length of tasks they could complete without human direction was also doubling about every eight months. The institute found vulnerabilities in every system it tested, while safeguards varied.

This is the central tension. Rules, warnings, and safety work are expanding. At the same time, companies and governments still want faster development and deployment.

【Point One】
Regulation is not one global brake. In the EU, duties for general-purpose model providers applied from 2 August 2025. Selected enforcement followed from 2 August 2026. Language models trained with more than 10^23 calculation steps are considered general-purpose models; above 10^25, a model is presumed to pose systemic risk, though that line is under review. The UN panel can assess the gap, but it cannot enforce a rule.

【Point Two】
One company reported releasing a new Flash model three weeks after its predecessor, with updated safeguards. Another said it held back larger Astra runs while raising safety and security requirements, then restarted the frontier run on 28 August 2026. It called for mandatory US testing and independent assessment. A third said industry-wide pacing would need a lawful, verifiable mechanism. US proposals range from rapid deployment to a temporary pause. These actions do not yet form a common brake.

point_one.reasoning: Full StoryのEU施行日やUNパネルの役割を補強しつつ、計算量10^23・10^25という分類基準と、その基準自体が見直し中である点を新たに示している。規制が単一の国際的な制動装置にならず、事業者にとって適用範囲やリスク判定が不確実だという具体的な意味も説明している。

point_two.reasoning: 複数企業のモデル投入・一時停止・再開、米国での義務的テストや一時停止案など、Full Storyにはない具体的な対応例を加えている。各社の安全策や政府案が共通の強制的な仕組みにまとまっておらず、現状では業界全体のペースを制御できないという実務的な示唆がある。
